# release-integrity-ignore.txt — tags that will never have a published release.
#
# Read by scripts/ci/check-release-integrity.sh. One `vX.Y.Z` tag per line;
# everything after `#` is a comment. Every entry MUST carry a reason.
#
# This file is an ignore list, not a floor. A floor tag ("only check >= vN")
# would be shorter, but it hides every gap beneath it — including gaps that
# appear later, if an old release is ever deleted. Ignoring tags one at a time,
# with a written reason, is the only form that keeps the record honest and
# keeps a new gap loud. A floor is also simply wrong for this repo: v0.56.0 and
# v0.57.0 are dead while v0.55.1 below them and v0.57.1 above them are both
# healthy, so no single cutoff separates good from bad.
#
# Adding an entry is a deliberate act. If you are adding one because a release
# failed, first ask whether the release can be re-run against the tag instead —
# a re-runnable failure is a bug to fix, not a line to add here.

# ── Empty releases from the 2026-08-05 → 2026-08-07 publish gap ──────────────
# tag-on-merge.yml creates the GitHub Release and then dispatches release.yml
# to upload the artifacts. When release.yml failed, the Release row was left
# behind with ZERO assets — which looks identical to a healthy release in the
# releases list, and is why this went unnoticed. Both were superseded.
#
# This is the exact shape the asset check exists to catch.
v0.56.0   # release.yml failed after the Release row was created; superseded by v0.57.1
v0.57.0   # same; superseded by v0.57.1

# ── Burned by the May 2026 release-pipeline migration ────────────────────────
# Version numbers consumed by release-pipeline iterations are real tags on the
# remote and cannot be reclaimed. See the "Note on burned version numbers"
# preamble in docs/roadmap.md and the "Burned tags" section of CLAUDE.md.
v0.7.0
v0.7.1
v0.7.2
v0.7.4
v0.7.5

# ── Pre-release-train archaeology ────────────────────────────────────────────
# v0.1.0 / v0.1.1 — cut before release.yml published GitHub Releases at all.
# v0.4.5          — release build failed; superseded by v0.5.0.
# v0.16.1         — release build failed; superseded by v0.17.0.
v0.1.0
v0.1.1
v0.4.5
v0.16.1
